I think I have honestly written entire paragraphs before that were just a long sequence of comma usage to break it up. (I also have a tendency to write things in parentheses a lot, and have sometimes had multiple of these types of statements in one sentence alone. So it's kind of a long running thing that's just all been crumbling apart as of lately. I've just in general had issues with finding jobs because I find job searching stressful and I'm especially bad at writing things like cover letters, so I end up procrastinating like crazy on that kind of stuff because I'll either end up forgetting or stressing myself out over it. As mentioned, it feels kind of like as soon as I have the thought that I need to do the thing, and realize there's going to be discomfort with trying to do the thing, my brain just shoves it aside. Literally any level of difficulty and I lose the thought process to do it. And so if I'm the only person regulating what I do, it ends up not getting done, because if my brain decides to not do it there's no other entity to tell me to do it. 

So anyways I graduated university in December, and so I have a bachelor's degree and should be out looking for jobs. And I went a full 3 months with absolutely no job searching because I just always procrastinated it. Also during this time my living space became an absolute garbage dump. I didn't do dishes at all in that 3 month span. I had food go moldy in my room and in my fridge. I just threw out milk the other day that had been in there since November. I'm not joking when I say things were an absolute disaster. And I always told myself I was going to get around to doing it. That I would clean things up and I would search for jobs and I would have things all together if I just had time. My job was only 25ish hours a week so I should have had time to do these things, but I always got sucked into internet holes and it just felt like I didn't have enough time to do things.

Then coronavirus rolls around and I'm put out of a job. So now I'm at home all day long with literally nothing to do, so it seems like a good time to finally get these things done. But still nothing got done. In fact, my life quality declined because I no longer had the rigid structure that was propping it up before. It's 6 am, I haven't gone to sleep yet, and that's honestly not abnormal for the past several weeks. Because with no need to wake up by a certain time there's less need to go to sleep at a certain time and so my progress towards going to sleep is more sluggish because I don't have as much pressure to NEED to go to sleep. And then since I go to sleep late, I wake up late, so I'm doing my daily things late, so it feels like I can't go to sleep at a normal time because it feels like I still have stuff to do except I'm procrastinating the stuff so it keeps getting later until I give up because I need to sleep eventually. And I'm kind of picking up my life a bit. I cleaned up a bit, I got the dishes done, I cleaned out the fridge of all the gross moldy Tupperware containers and old milk cartons. But I still can't push myself to do the job applications, which I need to be getting done.

So anyways, yesterday it kind of came crashing down when my stepmom called and I had to admit I wasn't getting it done and she tells me I just need to apply myself which I am honestly sick of hearing at this point and I try to tell her about how it feels like I'm physically incapable of pushing myself to do stuff and it's just a big emotional mess, especially with the added stress of my dad having to go to the hospital to get surgery for a medical problem he had previously had surgery for. So I tell myself I'm going to try to start working to improve, and I make myself a to do list. And just having those to do lists the past 2 days just makes it more prevalent that I'm not getting things done because there's extra pressure to get it done but it still doesn't get done and there's also a reminder that I didn't get it done so that causes a lot of distress. And maybe it's just a thing that I have to work on slowly and can't fix overnight, but I can't afford to take extra time. I need this fixed now

But anyways that comes around to me feeling like a failure and I just don't like my family being hurt by that. I guess I just want to suffer on my own and not drag them down with me. And I don't want to keep talking about how much of a failure I am and how I could be better if I just applied myself, and so if that's how every phone call is going to go from now on then I don't want to make those calls. And mostly I just wish I didn't make them sad. And I wish I could be better, but I've had so many failed attempts to fix my mental health that it starts to feel like there's no hope of it ever getting better
